clue.text: Variety act to get money from clubs in possession of European

parts.note: to tap someone is to get money from them

indicators.note: the European holds the clubs symbol, so one letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A music-hall turn sets out to fleece a European who carries clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like nightclubs or golf clubs, but it is the card suit, a single letter held by the European.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap routine is a classic turn on a variety bill, a stage show of mixed acts.

clue.text: Support back of ox, not rear of horse

indicators.note: back tells us to read the little word of from right to left
not tells us to leave out the letter named next from the ox word

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated ox

indicators.note: rear of points to the final letter of the word horse

explanation.surface: Instructions for propping up an ox from behind, not a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OF into FO; 'not rear of horse' removes E (the last letter of horse) from STEER, leaving STER.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is to encourage or nurture, a synonym of support.

clue.text: Suffer punishment, but appear invincible?

definitions.meaning: literally, to endure a number of blows
the idiom for something very hard to surpass or defeat

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally to be beaten and idiomatically to be hard to better.

clue.text: Youngster recalled difficult time, unable to take a breather

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the youngster word runs backwards

parts.note: a son is a youngster

indicators.note: unable to take means the following letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a trial is a difficult time
the letter A as written

explanation.surface: A youngster remembers a hard time when they could not catch their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SON into NOS; 'unable to take a' drops A from TRIAL, leaving TRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is an opening through which one breathes, so jokingly a breather.

clue.text: Not bright of colloquial speakers to dismiss old woman

indicators.note: dismiss means sending away the following letters from the longer word

parts.note: idiomatic describes the natural usage of native, colloquial speakers
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: Slangy talkers who send their mother packing are being dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss' removes MA from IDIOMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means stupid, the opposite of bright in the sense of clever.

clue.text: Seafood damage limited by French port, though not entirely

indicators.note: limited by means the damage word is held within the port's letters
not entirely means the port loses its final letter

parts.note: Calais is the French Channel port
to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: Seafood spoiled within reach of a French harbour, if only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid served as food, a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Miss opening of opera — singer taken aback about that

indicators.note: about means the singer word goes round the opening letter
taken aback read literally as taken backwards

parts.note: a diva is a star female singer

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of opera

explanation.surface: A soprano is startled to miss the start of the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns DIVA into AVID; 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to steer clear of it, to miss it deliberately.

clue.text: New look? Man dressed in black often needs it

parts.note: a football referee traditionally wears black
the word as written

explanation.surface: A remark that the referee in his black kit often needs a fresh image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'often needs' is linking padding; the referee joke works because referees are traditionally 'the man in black'.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit renovates and re-equips something, giving it a new look.

clue.text: Supporter is engaging in jokey comments

indicators.note: engaging in means the little word goes into the comments

parts.note: banter is playful, teasing talk
the word as written

explanation.surface: A fan takes part in some light-hearted joshing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but here it is the handrail on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is a stair handrail, something that supports you on the stairs.

clue.text: Animal suitable to board ark at sea? On the contrary

indicators.note: to board means going into something, here one word inside another
on the contrary swaps roles, so the jumbled ark goes inside the suitable word

parts.note: meet is an old word for suitable or fitting

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of ark are jumbled

explanation.surface: Is this creature fit to climb aboard a floating ark? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the surface: the scrambled ark goes into the suitable word, not the animal into the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A meerkat is a small burrowing mongoose of southern Africa, an animal.

clue.text: Briefly explain two cricketing terms

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run is a unit of scoring and an over is a set of six balls

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means recap quickly, and its two words are both cricket terms.

clue.text: I'd follow Oberon with minimum of grace in play?

definitions.text: I'd follow Oberon with minimum of grace in play?

indicators.note: in play hints at the letters being toyed with and rearranged
minimum of points to just the first letter of grace

explanation.surface: A fairy follows his king onstage with little elegance in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck, also called by this name, is the servant who follows the fairy king Oberon; the anagram fodder is the same words plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes Puck, the mischievous sprite who attends Oberon in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Snoop around organisation of women? Absolutely not

indicators.note: around means the snoop word encloses the women's organisation

parts.note: to nose is to pry or snoop
WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's community organisation

explanation.surface: A nosey parker hangs round a women's club and is firmly rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means in no way at all, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Very good to restrict visual activity before first showing of film

indicators.note: restrict means the very good word hems in the visual activity

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good
REM is rapid eye movement, eye activity during sleep
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A goody-goody stops someone looking around before a film opens.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) for very good is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public screening of a film.

clue.text: Major figures I erased from classic paintings?

indicators.note: erased from means the letter is rubbed out of the paintings word

parts.note: Titians are works by the Venetian Renaissance master Titian

explanation.surface: Has someone rubbed themself out of some old masterpieces?
explanation.walkthrough: 'erased from' removes one I from TITIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans are giants of their field, people of great stature or importance.

clue.text: Man chasing fish displaying weapon

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the man word follows the fish

parts.note: a pike is a predatory freshwater fish
to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: A fellow pursuing a fish brandishes a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb here, as in to man a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikestaff is the wooden shaft of a pike, an old infantry weapon.

clue.text: German drama missing first broadcast upset European country

indicators.note: missing first means the drama loses its opening letter

parts.note: Faust is Goethe's famous German verse drama

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the broadcast word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A German play lacking its opening is aired and causes a stir abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing first' trims FAUST to AUST; 'upset' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Beast of burden approached by inexperienced driver

parts.note: came means approached
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A pack animal is approached by a learner at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are used to carry loads, a classic beast of burden.

clue.text: Instrument, kind mostly found within confines of orchestra

indicators.note: found within means the kind word sits inside the orchestra's edges
confines of points to the outer letters of orchestra
mostly means the kind word loses its last letter

parts.note: caring means kind

explanation.surface: A musical instrument, a gentle one, is mostly heard inside the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the kind word, giving CARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.

clue.text: Eponymous hero in plot development

definitions.meaning: Oliver of the Dickens novel, whose surname gives the book its title
an unexpected turn in a story

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's title orphan bears this surname, and it also means an unexpected turn in a story.

clue.text: Wasting a sovereign

parts.note: wasting read as slang for killing, and sovereign as a monarch rather than a gold coin

explanation.definitionFit: Regicide is the murder of a king, and to waste someone is slang for killing them.

clue.text: Rock bands I love: I must be dancing!

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A rock fan insists on dancing to groups they adore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be dancing' rearranges BANDSIOI.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark volcanic glass, a type of igneous rock.

clue.text: Live extract being broadcast after one? That's the aim

indicators.note: after places the broadcast word behind the one

parts.note: am, as in I am, means exist or live
a bit is an extract or piece
I is the Roman numeral one
on means on air, being broadcast

explanation.surface: A live clip goes on air after the first item: that is the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is a goal or aim one strives for.

clue.text: Think too much of a revue composed with endless love

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
endless means the word love loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A critic is too fond of a revue written with boundless affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims LOVE to LOV; 'composed' rearranges AREVUELOV.
explanation.definitionFit: To overvalue is to rate something too highly.

clue.text: Boat raced after edging ahead initially

indicators.note: after puts the raced word behind the other pieces

parts.note: a trim is an edging or border

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of ahead

parts.note: ran means raced

explanation.surface: A boat sped off after nosing in front at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing vessel with three hulls.

clue.text: The money received cheers national leaders

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
kings lead nations

explanation.surface: The cash brought in delights the country's rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the receipts of a shop or business.

clue.text: Ray, a rafter, almost submerged at the outset

indicators.note: almost means the submerged word loses its last letter

parts.note: sunk means submerged; at the outset says this piece stands at the front of the answer
a beam is a rafter

explanation.surface: Ray, a roof timber, was nearly underwater at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the final K from the submerged word; 'at the outset' just says that piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of sunlight.

clue.text: Be about to go off to look for water around river

indicators.note: around means the water-seeking word encloses the river

parts.note: to dowse is to search for underground water with a rod
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Prepare to leave and go dowsing near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R inside DOWSE; 'go off' is nod off, not depart.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to be half asleep, about to drop off.

clue.text: Jog and shake, half-heartedly toppling over

indicators.note: toppling over in a down clue means the word is read backwards
half-heartedly means half of the double letter at the centre goes

parts.note: to wobble is to shake

explanation.surface: Running and quivering, someone half-heartedly falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one B from WOBBLE; 'toppling over' turns WOBLE round.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to nudge or jog them.

clue.text: Means to track bishop with grasp of computer language

indicators.note: grasp means the bishop letters hold the language

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
Ada is a programming language

explanation.surface: A bishop gets to grips with coding to follow something.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) for bishop is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a system for detecting and following objects such as aircraft.
